speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: My dear fellow, whom do I see! Ivan Vassilevitch! I am extremely glad! Now this is a surprise, my darling... How are you?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Thank you. And how may you be getting on?

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: We just get along somehow, my angel, to your prayers, and so on. Sit down, please do.... Now, you know, you shouldn’t forget all about your neighbours, my darling. My dear fellow, why are you so formal in your get-up? Evening dress, gloves, and so on. Can you be going anywhere, my treasure?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: No, I’ve come only to see you, honoured Stepan Stepanovitch.

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Then why are you in evening dress, my precious? As if you’re paying a New Year’s Eve visit!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Well, you see, it’s like this. I’ve come to you, honoured Stepan Stepanovitch, to trouble you with a request. Not once or twice have I already had the privilege of applying to you for help, and you have always, so to speak... I must ask your pardon, I am getting excited. I shall drink some water, honoured Stepan Stepanovitch.

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: He’s come to borrow money! Shan’t give him any! What is it, my beauty?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: You see, Honour Stepanitch... I beg pardon, Stepan Honouritch... I mean, I’m awfully excited, as you will please notice.... In short, you alone can help me, though I don’t deserve it, of course... and haven’t any right to count on your assistance....

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Oh, don’t go round and round it, darling! Spit it out! Well?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: One moment... this very minute. The fact is, I’ve come to ask the hand of your daughter, Natalya Stepanovna, in marriage.

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: By Jove! Ivan Vassilevitch! Say it again—I didn’t hear it all!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I have the honour to ask...

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: My dear fellow... I’m so glad, and so on.... Yes, indeed, and all that sort of thing. I’ve been hoping for it for a long time. It’s been my continual desire. And I’ve always loved you, my angel, as if you were my own son. May God give you both His help and His love and so on, and I did so much hope... What am I behaving in this idiotic way for? I’m off my balance with joy, absolutely off my balance! Oh, with all my soul... I’ll go and call Natasha, and all that.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Honoured Stepan Stepanovitch, do you think I may count on her consent?

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Why, of course, my darling, and... as if she won’t consent! She’s in love; egad, she’s like a love-sick cat, and so on.... Shan’t be long!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: It’s cold... I’m trembling all over, just as if I’d got an examination before me. The great thing is, I must have my mind made up. If I give myself time to think, to hesitate, to talk a lot, to look for an ideal, or for real love, then I’ll never get married.... Brr!... It’s cold! Natalya Stepanovna is an excellent housekeeper, not bad-looking, well-educated.... What more do I want? But I’m getting a noise in my ears from excitement. And it’s impossible for me not to marry.... In the first place, I’m already 35—a critical age, so to speak. In the second place, I ought to lead a quiet and regular life.... I suffer from palpitations, I’m excitable and always getting awfully upset.... At this very moment my lips are trembling, and there’s a twitch in my right eyebrow.... But the very worst of all is the way I sleep. I no sooner get into bed and begin to go off when suddenly something in my left side—gives a pull, and I can feel it in my shoulder and head.... I jump up like a lunatic, walk about a bit, and lie down again, but as soon as I begin to get off to sleep there’s another pull! And this may happen twenty times....

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Well, there! It’s you, and papa said, “Go; there’s a merchant come for his goods.” How do you do, Ivan Vassilevitch!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: How do you do, honoured Natalya Stepanovna?

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: You must excuse my apron and négligé... we’re shelling peas for drying. Why haven’t you been here for such a long time? Sit down. Won’t you have some lunch?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: No, thank you, I’ve had some already.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Then smoke.... Here are the matches.... The weather is splendid now, but yesterday it was so wet that the workmen didn’t do anything all day. How much hay have you stacked? Just think, I felt greedy and had a whole field cut, and now I’m not at all pleased about it because I’m afraid my hay may rot. I ought to have waited a bit. But what’s this? Why, you’re in evening dress! Well, I never! Are you going to a ball, or what?—though I must say you look better. Tell me, why are you got up like that?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: You see, honoured Natalya Stepanovna... the fact is, I’ve made up my mind to ask you to hear me out.... Of course you’ll be surprised and perhaps even angry, but a... It’s awfully cold!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: What’s the matter? Well?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I shall try to be brief. You must know, honoured Natalya Stepanovna, that I have long, since my childhood, in fact, had the privilege of knowing your family. My late aunt and her husband, from whom, as you know, I inherited my land, always had the greatest respect for your father and your late mother. The Lomovs and the Chubukovs have always had the most friendly, and I might almost say the most affectionate, regard for each other. And, as you know, my land is a near neighbour of yours. You will remember that my Oxen Meadows touch your birchwoods.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Excuse my interrupting you. You say, “my Oxen Meadows....” But are they yours?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Yes, mine.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: What are you talking about? Oxen Meadows are ours, not yours!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: No, mine, honoured Natalya Stepanovna.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Well, I never knew that before. How do you make that out?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: How? I’m speaking of those Oxen Meadows which are wedged in between your birchwoods and the Burnt Marsh.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Yes, yes.... They’re ours.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: No, you’re mistaken, honoured Natalya Stepanovna, they’re mine.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Just think, Ivan Vassilevitch! How long have they been yours?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: How long? As long as I can remember.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Really, you won’t get me to believe that!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: But you can see from the documents, honoured Natalya Stepanovna. Oxen Meadows, it’s true, were once the subject of dispute, but now everybody knows that they are mine. There’s nothing to argue about. You see, my aunt’s grandmother gave the free use of these Meadows in perpetuity to the peasants of your father’s grandfather, in return for which they were to make bricks for her. The peasants belonging to your father’s grandfather had the free use of the Meadows for forty years, and had got into the habit of regarding them as their own, when it happened that...

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: No, it isn’t at all like that! Both my grandfather and great-grandfather reckoned that their land extended to Burnt Marsh—which means that Oxen Meadows were ours. I don’t see what there is to argue about. It’s simply silly!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I’ll show you the documents, Natalya Stepanovna!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: No, you’re simply joking, or making fun of me.... What a surprise! We’ve had the land for nearly three hundred years, and then we’re suddenly told that it isn’t ours! Ivan Vassilevitch, I can hardly believe my own ears.... These Meadows aren’t worth much to me. They only come to five dessiatins , and are worth perhaps 300 roubles , but I can’t stand unfairness. Say what you will, but I can’t stand unfairness.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Hear me out, I implore you! The peasants of your father’s grandfather, as I have already had the honour of explaining to you, used to bake bricks for my aunt’s grandmother. Now my aunt’s grandmother, wishing to make them a pleasant...

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: I can’t make head or tail of all this about aunts and grandfathers and grandmothers! The Meadows are ours, and that’s all.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Mine.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Ours! You can go on proving it for two days on end, you can go and put on fifteen dress-jackets, but I tell you they’re ours, ours, ours! I don’t want anything of yours and I don’t want to give up anything of mine. So there!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Natalya Ivanovna, I don’t want the Meadows, but I am acting on principle. If you like, I’ll make you a present of them.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: I can make you a present of them myself, because they’re mine! Your behaviour, Ivan Vassilevitch, is strange, to say the least! Up to this we have always thought of you as a good neighbour, a friend: last year we lent you our threshing-machine, although on that account we had to put off our own threshing till November, but you behave to us as if we were gipsies. Giving me my own land, indeed! No, really, that’s not at all neighbourly! In my opinion, it’s even impudent, if you want to know....

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Then you make out that I’m a land-grabber? Madam, never in my life have I grabbed anybody else’s land, and I shan’t allow anybody to accuse me of having done so.... Oxen Meadows are mine!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: It’s not true, they’re ours!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Mine!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: It’s not true! I’ll prove it! I’ll send my mowers out to the Meadows this very day!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: What?

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: My mowers will be there this very day!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I’ll give it to them in the neck!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: You dare!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Oxen Meadows are mine! You understand? Mine!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Please don’t shout! You can shout yourself hoarse in your own house, but here I must ask you to restrain yourself!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: If it wasn’t, madam, for this awful, excruciating palpitation, if my whole inside wasn’t upset, I’d talk to you in a different way! Oxen Meadows are mine!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Ours!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Mine!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Ours!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Mine!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: What’s the matter? What are you shouting at?

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Papa, please tell to this gentleman who owns Oxen Meadows, we or he?

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Darling, the Meadows are ours!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: But, please, Stepan Stepanitch, how can they be yours? Do be a reasonable man! My aunt’s grandmother gave the Meadows for the temporary and free use of your grandfather’s peasants. The peasants used the land for forty years and got as accustomed to it as if it was their own, when it happened that...

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Excuse me, my precious.... You forget just this, that the peasants didn’t pay your grandmother and all that, because the Meadows were in dispute, and so on. And now everybody knows that they’re ours. It means that you haven’t seen the plan.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I’ll prove to you that they’re mine!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: You won’t prove it, my darling.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I shall!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Dear one, why yell like that? You won’t prove anything just by yelling. I don’t want anything of yours, and don’t intend to give up what I have. Why should I? And you know, my beloved, that if you propose to go on arguing about it, I’d much sooner give up the meadows to the peasants than to you. There!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I don’t understand! How have you the right to give away somebody else’s property?

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: You may take it that I know whether I have the right or not. Because, young man, I’m not used to being spoken to in that tone of voice, and so on: I, young man, am twice your age, and ask you to speak to me without agitating yourself, and all that.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: No, you just think I’m a fool and want to have me on! You call my land yours, and then you want me to talk to you calmly and politely! Good neighbours don’t behave like that, Stepan Stepanitch! You’re not a neighbour, you’re a grabber!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: What’s that? What did you say?

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Papa, send the mowers out to the Meadows at once!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: What did you say, sir?

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Oxen Meadows are ours, and I shan’t give them up, shan’t give them up, shan’t give them up!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: We’ll see! I’ll have the matter taken to court, and then I’ll show you!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: To court? You can take it to court, and all that! You can! I know you; you’re just on the look-out for a chance to go to court, and all that.... You pettifogger! All your people were like that! All of them!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Never mind about my people! The Lomovs have all been honourable people, and not one has ever been tried for embezzlement, like your grandfather!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: You Lomovs have had lunacy in your family, all of you!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: All, all, all!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Your grandfather was a drunkard, and your younger aunt, Nastasya Mihailovna, ran away with an architect, and so on.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: And your mother was hump-backed. Something pulling in my side.... My head.... Help! Water!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Your father was a guzzling gambler!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: And there haven’t been many backbiters to equal your aunt!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: My left foot has gone to sleep.... You’re an intriguer.... Oh, my heart!... And it’s an open secret that before the last elections you bri... I can see stars.... Where’s my hat?

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: It’s low! It’s dishonest! It’s mean!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: And you’re just a malicious, double-faced intriguer! Yes!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Here’s my hat.... My heart!... Which way? Where’s the door? Oh!... I think I’m dying.... My foot’s quite numb....

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: And don’t set foot in my house again!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Take it to court! We’ll see!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Devil take him!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: What a rascal! What trust can one have in one’s neighbours after that!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: The villain! The scarecrow!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: The monster! First he takes our land and then he has the impudence to abuse us.

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: And that blind hen, yes, that turnip-ghost has the confounded cheek to make a proposal, and so on! What? A proposal!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: What proposal?

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Why, he came here so as to propose to you.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: To propose? To me? Why didn’t you tell me so before?

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: So he dresses up in evening clothes. The stuffed sausage! The wizen-faced frump!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: To propose to me? Ah! Bring him back! Back! Ah! Bring him here.

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Bring whom here?

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Quick, quick! I’m ill! Fetch him!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: What’s that? What’s the matter with you? Oh, unhappy man that I am! I’ll shoot myself! I’ll hang myself! We’ve done for her!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: I’m dying! Fetch him!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Tfoo! At once. Don’t yell!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: What have they done to me! Fetch him back! Fetch him!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: He’s coming, and so on, devil take him! Ouf! Talk to him yourself; I don’t want to....

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Fetch him!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: He’s coming, I tell you. Oh, what a burden, Lord, to be the father of a grown-up daughter! I’ll cut my throat! I will, indeed! We cursed him, abused him, drove him out, and it’s all you... you!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: No, it was you!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: I tell you it’s not my fault. Now you talk to him yourself

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: My heart’s palpitating awfully.... My foot’s gone to sleep.... There’s something keeps pulling in my side.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Forgive us, Ivan Vassilevitch, we were all a little heated.... I remember now: Oxen Meadows really are yours.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: My heart’s beating awfully.... My Meadows.... My eyebrows are both twitching....

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: The Meadows are yours, yes, yours.... Do sit down.... We were wrong....

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I did it on principle.... My land is worth little to me, but the principle...

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Yes, the principle, just so.... Now let’s talk of something else.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: The more so as I have evidence. My aunt’s grandmother gave the land to your father’s grandfather’s peasants...

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Yes, yes, let that pass.... I wish I knew how to get him started.... Are you going to start shooting soon?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I’m thinking of having a go at the blackcock, honoured Natalya Stepanovna, after the harvest. Oh, have you heard? Just think, what a misfortune I’ve had! My dog Guess, whom you know, has gone lame.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: What a pity! Why?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I don’t know.... Must have got twisted, or bitten by some other dog.... My very best dog, to say nothing of the expense. I gave Mironov 125 roubles for him.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: It was too much, Ivan Vassilevitch.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I think it was very cheap. He’s a first-rate dog.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Papa gave 85 roubles for his Squeezer, and Squeezer is heaps better than Guess!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Squeezer better than. Guess? What an idea! Squeezer better than Guess!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Of course he’s better! Of course, Squeezer is young, he may develop a bit, but on points and pedigree he’s better than anything that even Volchanetsky has got.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Excuse me, Natalya Stepanovna, but you forget that he is overshot, and an overshot always means the dog is a bad hunter!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Overshot, is he? The first time I hear it!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I assure you that his lower jaw is shorter than the upper.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Have you measured?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Yes. He’s all right at following, of course, but if you want him to get hold of anything...

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: In the first place, our Squeezer is a thoroughbred animal, the son of Harness and Chisels, while there’s no getting at the pedigree of your dog at all.... He’s old and as ugly as a worn-out cab-horse.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: He is old, but I wouldn’t take five Squeezers for him.... Why, how can you?... Guess is a dog; as for Squeezer, well, it’s too funny to argue.... Anybody you like has a dog as good as Squeezer... you may find them under every bush almost. Twenty-five roubles would be a handsome price to pay for him.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: There’s some demon of contradiction in you to-day, Ivan Vassilevitch. First you pretend that the Meadows are yours; now, that Guess is better than Squeezer. I don’t like people who don’t say what they mean, because you know perfectly well that Squeezer is a hundred times better than your silly Guess. Why do you want to say it isn’t?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I see, Natalya Stepanovna, that you consider me either blind or a fool. You must realize that Squeezer is overshot!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: It’s not true.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: He is!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: It’s not true!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Why shout, madam?

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Why talk rot? It’s awful! It’s time your Guess was shot, and you compare him with Squeezer!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Excuse me; I cannot continue this discussion: my heart is palpitating.

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: I’ve noticed that those hunters argue most who know least.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Madam, please be silent.... My heart is going to pieces.... Shut up!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: I shan’t shut up until you acknowledge that Squeezer is a hundred times better than your Guess!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: A hundred times worse! Be hanged to your Squeezer! His head... eyes... shoulder...

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: There’s no need to hang your silly Guess; he’s half-dead already!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Shut up! My heart’s bursting!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: I shan’t shut up.

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: What’s the matter now?

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Papa, tell us truly, which is the better dog, our Squeezer or his Guess.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Stepan Stepanovitch, I implore you to tell me just one thing: is your Squeezer overshot or not? Yes or no?

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: And suppose he is? What does it matter? He’s the best dog in the district for all that, and so on.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: But isn’t my Guess better? Really, now?

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Don’t excite yourself, my precious one.... Allow me.... Your Guess certainly has his good points.... He’s pure-bred, firm on his feet, has well-sprung ribs, and all that. But, my dear man, if you want to know the truth, that dog has two defects: he’s old and he’s short in the muzzle.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Excuse me, my heart.... Let’s take the facts.... You will remember that on the Marusinsky hunt my Guess ran neck-and-neck with the Count’s dog, while your Squeezer was left a whole verst behind.

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: He got left behind because the Count’s whipper-in hit him with his whip.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: And with good reason. The dogs are running after a fox, when Squeezer goes and starts worrying a sheep!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: It’s not true!... My dear fellow, I’m very liable to lose my temper, and so, just because of that, let’s stop arguing. You started because everybody is always jealous of everybody else’s dogs. Yes, we’re all like that! You too, sir, aren’t blameless! You no sooner notice that some dog is better than your Guess than you begin with this, that... and the other... and all that.... I remember everything!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I remember too!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: I remember, too.... What do you remember?

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: My heart... my foot’s gone to sleep.... I can’t...

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: My heart.... What sort of a hunter are you? You ought to go and lie on the kitchen oven and catch blackbeetles, not go after foxes! My heart!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Yes really, what sort of a hunter are you, anyway? You ought to sit at home with your palpitations, and not go tracking animals. You could go hunting, but you only go to argue with people and interfere with their dogs and so on. Let’s change the subject in case I lose my temper. You’re not a hunter at all, anyway!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: And are you a hunter? You only go hunting to get in with the Count and to intrigue.... Oh, my heart!... You’re an intriguer!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: What? I an intriguer? Shut up!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Intriguer!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Boy! Pup!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Old rat! Jesuit!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Shut up or I’ll shoot you like a partridge! You fool!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Everybody knows that—oh my heart!—your late wife used to beat you.... My feet... temples... sparks.... I fall, I fall!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: And you’re under the slipper of your housekeeper!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: There, there, there... my heart’s burst! My shoulder’s come off.... Where is my shoulder? I die. A doctor!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Boy! Milksop! Fool! I’m sick! Sick!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: What sort of a hunter are you? You can’t even sit on a horse! Papa, what’s the matter with him? Papa! Look, papa! Ivan Vassilevitch! He’s dead!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: I’m sick!... I can’t breathe!... Air!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: He’s dead. Ivan Vassilevitch! Ivan Vassilevitch! What have you done to me? He’s dead. A doctor, a doctor!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Oh!... What is it? What’s the matter?

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: He’s dead... dead!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Who’s dead? So he is! My word! Water! A doctor! Drink this!... No, he doesn’t drink.... It means he’s dead, and all that.... I’m the most unhappy of men! Why don’t I put a bullet into my brain? Why haven’t I cut my throat yet? What am I waiting for? Give me a knife! Give me a pistol! He seems to be coming round.... Drink some water! That’s right....

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: I see stars... mist.... Where am I?

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Hurry up and get married and—well, to the devil with you! She’s willing! She’s willing and all that. I give you my blessing and so on. Only leave me in peace!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Eh? What? To whom?

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: She’s willing! Well? Kiss and be damned to you!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: He’s alive... Yes, yes, I’m willing....

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Kiss each other!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Eh? Kiss whom? Very nice, too. Excuse me, what’s it all about? Oh, now I understand... my heart... stars... I’m happy. Natalya Stepanovna.... My foot’s gone to sleep....

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: I... I’m happy too....

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: What a weight off my shoulders.... Ouf!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: But... still you will admit now that Guess is worse than Squeezer.

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: Better!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Worse!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Well, that’s a way to start your family bliss! Have some champagne!

speeches.speaker: LOMOV
speeches.text: He’s better!

speeches.speaker: NATALYA STEPANOVNA
speeches.text: Worse! worse! worse!

speeches.speaker: CHUBUKOV
speeches.text: Champagne! Champagne!
